newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold trade depressed by smuggled bullion.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold trade depressed by smuggled bullion.

text.p: South Korean domestic gold prices rose slightly but demand for imported gold was seen pressured by an influx of smuggled bullion over the past week, traders in Seoul said on Tuesday.
"Imported gold demand is depressed by the arrival of smuggled gold," said a trader with a major bullion trade house, who asked not to be identified.

The trader said it was hard to determine the amount of gold smuggled into the domestic market recently, but it has been believed that the smuggled bullion constitutes more than 80 percent of the country's total demand.
The trader said the smuggled gold was offered at a discount of about 2,000 won per 3.75 grams, compared to imported gold.
Gold brought into South Korea through official channels is subject to a three percent import tariff and 10 percent value-added tax at the point of sale.

The flow of smuggled gold into South Korea has slowed since mid-February when internal security was tightened in response to the fatal shooting of North Korean defector Li Il-nam, a nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's ex-wife.

Domestic gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, rose on Tuesday to 10,250 won per gram from 10,200 won a week ago.
The company's silver price also rose slightly to 151 won a gram from 150 won a week earlier.

Several traders said a slowdown in the domestic economy following the collapse of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel and continued worries about payment defaults by local companies would depress gold demand.

The Korea Exchange Bank posted on Tuesday the telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers at 894.80 won against the dollar, unchanged from a week ago. The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for companies.
